Here Penny was leading Les Cohen by 39 secs., with Allum a further 20 secs. behind in third place. Williams, Taylor, Ring, Shields and Flower followed.
Soon after this, Bert forged ahead to pass Carter, Flower came up from 10th position to 7th to displace Allum, and Shields dropped back a couple of places.

Allum was soon to the front, with Parker in close attendance, and this remained the position until a mile to go. Then a leg injury of Parker's asserted itself, and he began to drop places sensationally.

A small bunch of four runners gradually left the rest of the field, these being Carter, Penny, Cohen and Allum. It soon became a question of who would crack first; and Allum was seen to be slowly falling behind.

Allum assumed second place, followed by Stimpson, but they were too far behind to make any impression on Bain. Stimpson eventually took second place, and Footer, running through the field, came into fourth place.
At the end of the stage we still led, but our margin was much reduced. Arthur Allum was our last representative. He had nine seconds lead from Birchfield and eleven seconds from Mitcham.
